In [[mathematics]], the '''Brauer–Suzuki theorem''', proved by {{harvtxt|Brauer|Suzuki|1959}}, {{harvtxt|Suzuki|1962}}, {{harvtxt|Brauer|1964}}, states that if a [[finite group]] has a [[generalized quaternion group|generalized quaternion]] [[Sylow subgroup|Sylow 2-subgroup]] and no non-trivial [[normal subgroup]]s of [[parity (mathematics)|odd]] [[order (group theory)|order]], then the group has a [[center (group theory)|center]] of order 2. In particular, such a group cannot be [[simple group|simple]].

A generalization of the Brauer–Suzuki theorem is given by [[George Glauberman|Glauberman]]'s [[Z* theorem]].
